title: P1: redirect()/revalidatePath() are called inside the withTenantScope body at 13+ real server actions, and nothing states or enforces the invariant
why_open: apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:135 calls redirect(`/messages/${convo.id}`) as the last statement INSIDE `withTenantScope(userId, async () => {...})` (opened at line ~90); same shape at messages/actions.ts:190,224,255,319, admin/actions.ts:73, calendar/actions.ts:168, orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:113 and :214, orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:490, plus ~45 revalidatePath() calls inside scope bodies (admin/actions.ts:499-501,896-898; feed/actions.ts:51,84,154,233; orgs/actions.ts:46,102-104,142-144,159-161; resources/actions.ts:68-69,85-86; settings/actions.ts:164,190; members/actions.ts:121,189; memory/actions.ts:62). redirect() is a Next.js control-flow THROW. Today withTenantScope is AsyncLocalStorage-only (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:84 `storage.run`), so the throw is currently survivable — but PLATFORM-ARCHITECTURE's withTenant is `db.$transaction` + `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id`, and the moment that lands every one of these silently rolls back its write while the user sees a successful navigation. No test, lint rule or architecture test asserts the invariant: `grep -rn redirect tests/` returns only no-host-derived-urls.test.mjs (a different concern). The only near-miss is apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.test.ts:247-261, which asserts the OPPOSITE ("lets the body's error out unchanged") using `throw new Error("NEXT_REDIRECT")` — a plain Error with NO `digest`, so a guard keyed on `digest` leaves that test green.
smallest_real_change: (a) In apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts, wrap the `runInTenantScope(scope, () => fn(scope))` call in withTenantScope/withSystemTenantScope with a catch that inspects `(err as {digest?:string}).digest?.startsWith('NEXT_REDIRECT')` or `=== 'NEXT_NOT_FOUND'` and rethrows a TenantContextError naming the file and the invariant ('redirect() and revalidatePath() must be called after the scope closes; inside a transactional scope they abort the transaction and roll the write back'). Key it on `digest`, NOT on the message — apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.test.ts:258 throws a bare Error('NEXT_REDIRECT') and must stay green. (b) Change the shape of the real call sites from `await withTenantScope(uid, async () => { ...; redirect(x) })` to `const to = await withTenantScope(uid, async () => { ...; return x }); redirect(to)` — and hoist revalidatePath the same way. (c) Add tests/architecture/redirect-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs that parses every apps/web/src/app/**/actions.ts, tracks paren depth from each `withTenantScope(`/`withSystemTenantScope(` opening, and fails on any `redirect(`/`revalidatePath(`/`notFound(` at depth > 0. MUTATION TO PROVE IT: move `redirect(to)` back inside one scope body — both the unit guard and the architecture test must red; restore and both pass. Skip apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/** entirely (owned by another run) but leave the architecture test covering it so their fix is required too. Also state the second half of finding #16 in tenant-scope.ts's header: React.cache() is per-request, not per-scope. Audited today and NOT violated — every cache()d loader is either keyed by institutionId (config/server.ts:34,62,89,136; institution-time.ts:17; tenancy/locale-cookie.ts:50) or runs runUnscoped and is keyed by userId (rbac.ts:42, tenant-scope.ts:58) — so the change is to write the rule down beside the cache() calls it governs, not to move code.

title: The transactional outbox has no runner: every ApprovalRequested/ApprovalDecided row ever written is stranded at state='pending' forever
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:140 `dispatchOnce`, :212 `replay`, :116 MAX_ATTEMPTS, :126 backoffMs and :251 RETRYABLE_STATES have ZERO production callers — a repo-wide grep for `dispatchOnce|OutboxPorts|RETRYABLE_STATES` outside apps/web/src/lib/outbox/{outbox.ts,outbox.test.ts} returns nothing in apps/, infrastructure/, tools/, .github/ or tests/. Meanwhile apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:154 and :436 really do write OutboxEvent rows inside the deciding transaction, and apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1088-1118 carries state/attempts/availableAt/deadLetteredAt plus `@@index([state, availableAt])` whose own comment reads 'The dispatcher's only query'. The codebase already confesses it: modules/index.ts:512 records `['commands-events-and-idempotency','gap', ... ,'Nothing delivers that event yet: dispatchOnce takes a `deliver` port and no runner supplies one, so the consumption is declared and not running.']`, and modules/index.ts:539 declares the memory module `consumes: ['ApprovalDecided']`. So the chain modules/index.ts:771-773 declares (approvals -> approvals -> memory) is a declaration with no runtime. WRK-060-003's checkpoints, throttling, fairness and outage recovery have no home at all: `claimDue(now, limit)` (outbox.ts:94) is a single global claim, so one busy institution's backlog starves every other tenant's events.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts implementing OutboxPorts against db.outboxEvent: `claimDue` = an atomic `UPDATE ... SET state='dispatching' WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... WHERE state IN ('pending') AND availableAt <= now ORDER BY availableAt LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` (SKIP LOCKED is what makes two runners not claim the same row, which outbox.ts:90 requires); markDispatched/scheduleRetry/deadLetter are single updates. Add apps/web/src/lib/outbox/subscribers.ts holding the real `deliver` port: a Map from event type to handler, seeded with the ONE subscription modules/index.ts:539 already declares — ApprovalDecided -> write the decision into MemoryRecord via apps/web/src/lib/memory.ts — and refusing to deliver an event to a module that does not declare `consumes` for it (that refusal is the loop prevention: a handler may not emit the type it consumed). Add apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts modelled exactly on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts (JOB_SECRET bearer check, parseJobRequest envelope, `forEachInstitution` for the pass) — driving the pass per-institution IS the fairness requirement, because each tenant gets its own bounded claim instead of competing for one global LIMIT. Extend outbox.ts only with a per-pass `maxPerTenant` so a claim cannot be starved. TESTS TO PROVE: (1) an .itest against the running Postgres that writes two OutboxEvent rows in different institutions, runs the route handler, and asserts BOTH became state='dispatched' and a MemoryRecord exists — mutate by making `deliver` a no-op that never records and confirm it reds; (2) an idempotency test that runs the pass twice and asserts exactly one MemoryRecord; (3) a fairness test with 200 rows in institution A and 1 in institution B asserting B's row is dispatched in the same pass — mutate by replacing forEachInstitution with a single global claim and confirm it reds. Finally flip modules/index.ts:512 from 'gap' to 'pass' with the route path as evidence — that line is currently TRUE, so it must not be edited before the runner exists.

title: Sign-in interruption discards the task: every guarded surface redirects to a bare /signin and sign-in always lands on /dashboard, so a deep link is silently lost
why_open: apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx:34 hardcodes `redirectTo: "/dashboard"` in the sign-in server action, and page.tsx:22 sends an already-signed-in visitor to /dashboard regardless of where they were going. Thirty-one guarded entry points throw the destination away: apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:25, admin/layout.tsx:16, apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:21, dashboard/page.tsx:35, calendar/page.tsx:53, calendar/[id]/page.tsx:22, messages/[id]/page.tsx:61, orgs/[slug]/finance/page.tsx:23, orgs/[slug]/documents/[id]/view/page.tsx:26, search/page.tsx:28, settings/page.tsx:18 and 25, resources/[slug]/page.tsx:22, reports/finance/page.tsx:25 etc. — all `redirect("/signin")` with no return path, and searchParams on the sign-in page is read only for `error` (page.tsx:27). There is no return-path helper anywhere: grep for `callbackUrl` in apps/web/src finds only lib/auth.ts:163 `pages: { signIn: "/signin" }`. So a member who follows an emailed link to /approvals/abc or /orgs/x/finance signs in and lands on the dashboard with no way back — the exact 'interruption and exact safe task resumption' WRK-030-003 names.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/lib/http/return-path.ts beside internal-headers.ts with two functions: `signInPathFor(pathname, search?)` returning `/signin?next=<encoded>`, and `safeReturnPath(raw): string` that returns '/dashboard' unless the value is a same-origin app path — must start with a single '/', must NOT start with '//' or '/\\', must contain no scheme (reject anything matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i even after decoding), must not be '/signin' (a loop), and must be decoded ONCE then re-validated so '%2F%2Fevil.test' cannot slip through. Call `signInPathFor` from apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:21 and apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:25 (the two chokepoints every guarded page passes through), and in apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx replace the hardcoded `redirectTo: "/dashboard"` with `redirectTo: safeReturnPath(next)` where `next` is read from the searchParams the page already awaits at line 27, and make line 22's already-signed-in redirect use the same value. TESTS TO PROVE: a unit table over `//evil.test`, `https://evil.test`, `/\\evil.test`, `java%0ascript:alert(1)`, `%2f%2fevil.test`, `/signin?next=/signin`, and a legitimate `/orgs/consulting/finance` — asserting the first six collapse to '/dashboard' and the last survives; plus a Playwright spec that visits /orgs/<slug>/finance signed out, signs in with the dev-login form, and asserts the final URL is /orgs/<slug>/finance. MUTATION: change `safeReturnPath` to return `raw` unchanged — the open-redirect table must red; change it to always return '/dashboard' — the Playwright resumption spec must red. This is the same file area as the redirect/withTenantScope item and should be implemented by the same agent.

title: Relationships carry no provenance and nothing ever populates them: the entire ReBAC branch of the authorization engine is unreachable in production
why_open: packages/authorization/src/decide.ts:68 declares `relationships?: readonly Relationship[]` on the authorization world — OPTIONAL — and the branches that read it (decide.ts:288, :295, :306, :433 `hasRelationship(...)`) therefore never fire, because the ONLY production constructor of an AuthorizationWorld, apps/web/src/lib/authz/seat-world.ts:88-97 (`seatWorld`) and :180 (`institutionWorld`), returns `{ principals, memberships, roles, grants, enabledModules, entitlements }` with no `relationships` key at all. `grep -rn 'relationships:' apps/web/src` returns nothing. This is exactly the silent-optional-field failure mode: tsc is happy, every unit test passes because packages/authorization/src/*.test.ts build their own worlds with relationships in them, and in the running app MANAGES/ADVISES/OWNS/PARTICIPATES_IN decide nothing. Separately, packages/authorization/src/relationships.ts:62-72 `Relationship` has type/from/to/tenantId and `Dated` start-end only — there is no provenance discriminator, no confidence, no reviewedAt and no review expiry, so an edge inferred from a roster join is indistinguishable from one a Director asserted, which is precisely what WRK-010-002 requires.
smallest_real_change: In packages/authorization/src/relationships.ts add a REQUIRED `provenance: { origin: 'ASSERTED' | 'INFERRED' | 'IMPORTED'; source: string; confidence: number; reviewedAt: string | null; reviewExpiresAt: string | null }` to `Relationship`, and make `relationshipHoldsAt` (relationships.ts:111) return false for an INFERRED edge whose `reviewExpiresAt` has passed or whose confidence is below a stated floor — so an unreviewed inference decays instead of becoming permanent authority, the same argument relationships.ts:56-61 already makes for end dates. Because the field is REQUIRED, fix every construction site in the same change: `grep -rn 'type: "MANAGES"\|type: "HOLDS_SEAT_IN"\|type: "OWNS"\|type: "ADVISES"\|type: "OVERSEES"\|type: "PARTICIPATES_IN"\|type: "COLLABORATES_WITH"' packages apps` — today that is packages/authorization/src/relationships.test.ts, rebac-assurance.test.ts and decide.ts's own tests only, so the blast radius is provable. Then give the branch a real caller: add `relationshipsFor(ctx, tenantId)` to apps/web/src/lib/authz/seat-world.ts deriving INFERRED edges from data the app already loads in getUserContext (rbac.ts:42) — HOLDS_SEAT_IN from each live orgRole, OWNS from ApprovalRequest.requestedById — each stamped `origin:'INFERRED'`, `source:'RoleAssignment'`/`'ApprovalRequest'`, and a review expiry, and include it in BOTH the seatWorld return at seat-world.ts:88 and the institutionWorld spread at :180 (that second one is the caller a widening would otherwise miss). MUTATION TO PROVE: drop `relationships` from institutionWorld's return only — a decide() test asserting a requester may withdraw their own request through institutionWorld must red while the seatWorld one stays green; and set an INFERRED edge's reviewExpiresAt into the past and assert the permission is refused.

title: Execution-time reauthorization exists only as an uncalled module, and its idempotency replay can return a different request's result because requestDigest defaults to the empty string
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:86 `dispatch` is the only place the codebase reauthorizes at execution (bus.ts:167 `ports.authorize(context, command)`), and it has NO production caller — `grep -rn 'lib/commands' apps/web/src` returns nothing outside bus.ts and bus.test.ts. Every real write instead authorizes at render time and never rechecks. Worse, bus.ts:90 declares `options: { requestDigest: string; idempotencyTtlMs?: number } = { requestDigest: "" }`: a caller that omits options claims the key with digest "", so bus.ts:130 `replayable(claim.existing, "")` compares "" against "" and returns TRUE for a genuinely different request that reused the key — the exact outcome bus.ts:125-127's own comment says must never happen ('returning the earlier result would tell the caller something untrue about a request that never ran'). There is also no plan digest: nothing compares the plan a request was approved against with the plan being executed, so WRK-050-003's 'invalidate approval after meaningful plan or authority change' has no mechanism.
smallest_real_change: Two parts, one of which is unblocked today. UNBLOCKED: delete the `= { requestDigest: "" }` default at bus.ts:90 so `options` is required, and refuse an empty/whitespace digest with a `validation` ContractError before claiming the key — an empty digest is not a digest, and a caller that has none must be made to say so. Add the plan-digest half in the same function: carry `approvedDigest` on the command context and refuse with a new `authorization.plan-changed` ContractError when it disagrees with `options.requestDigest`, so an approval granted for one plan cannot execute a different one. Prove with a bus.test.ts case that claims a key with digest 'A', then dispatches the same key with digest 'B', and asserts `idempotency.key-reused` rather than a replayed success — MUTATION: restore the `""` default and call dispatch without options in that test; it must red. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL for the caller: wiring `dispatch` to a real write path needs an IdempotencyRecord table and apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma is owned by another cluster run this session — name that file rather than editing it. The natural first caller once the table exists is apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/reschedule/route.ts (a mutating route that today authorizes once and has no idempotency key); the approvals path is the other obvious one but apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts and apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/** are also owned by another run.

title: Provider review/verification/marketplace status is not modelled at all, and the catalog activation gate that does exist has no production caller
why_open: packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts models Tenure's OWN certification (`CatalogCertification` at :107, `certificationState` at :354, `isUsable` at :393, `availabilityDecisions` at :562, `availableToTenants` at :596) and nothing about the PROVIDER side — there is no field anywhere for Google OAuth app verification state, Microsoft publisher verification, a Slack app-directory distribution status or a marketplace listing state, which is what WRK-040-003 requires as an activation gate. `ConnectorEntry` (catalogs.ts:194) carries only kind/egressHosts/compatibility. And the gate is inert: `grep -rn 'isUsable|availableToTenants|availabilityDecisions|CATALOG_ENTRIES|certificationState' apps/web/src` returns NOTHING — the only hits outside catalogs.ts are the re-exports at packages/provisioning/src/index.ts:152-160. So the one shipped connector, RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR (catalogs.ts:631), is honestly marked uncertified with a disclaimer nobody reads at runtime, while apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:118 decides `available = flag.enabled && aiConfigured() && mayRetrieve` — the connector's own gate is not one of the three terms.
smallest_real_change: Add `providerReview?: { program: string; state: 'NOT_SUBMITTED'|'IN_REVIEW'|'APPROVED'|'REJECTED'|'EXPIRED'; approvedScopes: readonly string[]; verifiedAt: string | null; expiresAt: string | null }` to `ConnectorEntry` (catalogs.ts:194) plus `requestedScopes: readonly string[]`, and extend `isUsable` (catalogs.ts:393) with two new UsabilityReasons: `provider-review-missing` when a connector reaches PUBLISHED with no APPROVED providerReview, and `scopes-exceed-provider-approval` when requestedScopes is not a subset of approvedScopes — the second is the one that earns its place, because a connector can be Tenure-certified and still be asking for scopes the provider never approved. Update the single construction site RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR (catalogs.ts:631) honestly: no provider review has happened, so it gets `state:'NOT_SUBMITTED'` and starts failing the new gate for a stated reason rather than passing by omission. Then give the gate a production caller: in apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts compute `isUsable(RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR, now)` and report it as a THIRD, separately-named field beside `aiDisabledReason` and `toolRefusal` — the route already refuses to collapse distinct reasons (route.ts:110-117), so `connectorRefusal` belongs in the same response. BE HONEST ABOUT THE CONSEQUENCE: making that term part of `available` at route.ts:118 will stop the vendor call everywhere, because the connector genuinely is uncertified — that is what catalogs.ts:620-629 says should happen, and it will red any e2e that asserts a prose answer, so run the AI specs and either fix them or record the behaviour change deliberately. MUTATION: give RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR an APPROVED providerReview whose approvedScopes omit one requestedScope and assert `scopes-exceed-provider-approval`; widen approvedScopes and confirm it passes.

title: Not one module has an SLO, an alert or a runbook — every manifest records the observability dimension as a gap, and there is no evaluator to make one true
why_open: packages/module-runtime/src/manifest.ts:98 declares `observability-slo-and-finops` as a required completeness dimension, and every single module in modules/index.ts records it as a gap: lines 162, 206, 250, 294, 348, 392, 446, 522, 578, 636, 667 and 710 — twelve modules, twelve gaps, with reasons like 'No SLO, alert or runbook for roster availability' and (line 294) 'apps/web/src/lib/approvals-sla.ts computes an SLA per request. Nothing alerts on the aggregate, so a queue that has stopped moving is visible only to whoever opens it.' There is no SLO type, no objective, no error budget and no evaluator anywhere in the tree: `grep -rln 'errorBudget|error_budget'` over apps/, packages/ and infrastructure/ returns only vendored terraform provider binaries. So WRK-120-003's SLOs, alerts, escalation and outage controls are entirely unbuilt, and the manifest dimension is the honest record of it.
smallest_real_change: Start with the ONE module whose measurement already exists rather than inventing twelve. Add an `slo?: { objective: string; target: number; window: string; measure: string; runbook: string }[]` to the module manifest type in packages/module-runtime/src/manifest.ts, and declare one real objective on the approvals module in modules/index.ts — 'a pending approval is decided within its SLA' — pointing `measure` at apps/web/src/lib/approvals-sla.ts, which per modules/index.ts:294 already computes exactly that per request. Then build the evaluator and give it a caller: an `sloBurn(measurements, objective)` in module-runtime returning attained/target/burn, called from a new branch of apps/web/src/app/api/health/route.ts (or a /api/jobs/slo route modelled on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts, using forEachInstitution so the burn is per tenant, which is what WRK-120-003's 'provider/tenant/capability SLOs' means) that aggregates open ApprovalRequest ages and reports whether the objective is met. MUTATION TO PROVE: seed approvals that breach the SLA and assert the endpoint reports the objective as breached with the runbook path; then freeze `sloBurn` to return a constant and confirm the endpoint test reds — assert on the value the ROUTE emits, not on sloBurn called directly. Only after the endpoint is real may modules/index.ts:294 flip from 'gap'; the other eleven lines stay 'gap' because they still are.

title: A Relay tool refusal is a dead end: the chat route returns the engine's reason and no path to fix it, so 'missing access' has no low-friction route to access
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:110-122 builds `RefusedTool { toolKey, requiredPermission, reason }` and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:151-155 returns it as a bare `toolRefusal` string. That is the 'honest' half of WRK-GATE-030 and none of the 'low-friction path' half: the response names no one who could grant the permission, offers no request route, and distinguishes 'this system does not run that module' from 'you personally may not' only in prose the client cannot branch on. There is no ConnectionOpportunity, no PendingActionIntent and no remediation type anywhere — `grep -rn 'ConnectionOpportunity|PendingActionIntent|ConnectionLaunchToken' apps packages` returns nothing. apps/web/src/lib/admin/capabilities.ts already knows which capability each admin action needs, so the information to say 'ask a Director for search.index.query' exists and is not joined up.
smallest_real_change: Widen `RefusedTool` (relay-tools.ts:44-51) with a required discriminated `remedy`: `{ kind: 'MODULE_NOT_INSTALLED', module }` when relayToolsFor returned no such registration for this system, vs `{ kind: 'PERMISSION_NOT_HELD', requiredPermission, grantedByRoles }` when decideCheck refused — the two are produced in different branches of authorizeRelayTools today (the early return at relay-tools.ts:86 and the refused.push at :110) and are currently indistinguishable to the caller. Resolve `grantedByRoles` from ROLE_TEMPLATES, which packages/authorization already exports and seat-world.ts:94 already uses, so the answer is derived from the real catalog and never a hardcoded string. Return the structured remedy from apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts alongside the existing `toolRefusal` string (keep the string — the existing client renders it). TESTS TO PROVE: extend apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.test.ts (which already exercises 'rochester' with search.corpus and 'midtown-arts' with none) to assert the two remedy kinds are different for those two tenants, and add a route test asserting the field reaches the response body. MUTATION: collapse both branches to one remedy kind and confirm the tenant-vs-principal test reds. NOTE the boundary: the Connection Center surface that would render this lives under apps/web/src/components, which is owned by another cluster run this session — do not build the UI here; ship the API contract and leave the surface to WRK-110-002.
